advances: Unbounded unrestricted container volume for a fixed positive-dimensional depth region above its actual mixed maximum.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The region $D$ is the intersection of the closed halfspaces of $\mu$-mass greater than $4/5$. A point outside such a halfspace has a containing closed parallel halfspace in its open complement, hence depth less than $1/5$. Conversely, the open complement of a closed containing halfspace of mass less than $1/5$ is exhausted by closed parallel halfspaces and one of them has mass greater than $4/5$. This proves the intersection description. Separation gives $D\subseteq C$, so $D$ is compact and convex.

For a binary vertex $v$ set $q_v(z)=\sum_{j=1}^2[(1-v_j)z_j+v_j(1-z_j)]$. This is an affine function on the ambient base, zero at $v$ and at least one at each other binary vertex. At $(v,x_0)$ choose $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$ with $\sigma x_0\ge0$. The cap $\sigma x-3q_v(z)\ge \sigma x_0$ sees only the fiber at $v$, and there it captures length at most one. At $(v,0)$ every containing closed halfspace pays length at least one in that fiber, so the maximum mixed depth is exactly $1/8$ and $D$ misses all mixed points.

At the mark with base any edge midpoint of the square and continuous coordinate zero, the two fibers on that edge have total probability $1/2$ and are centrally symmetric about the mark. They pay at least $1/4$ in every containing cap, and a horizontal half-interval cut with a tilt excluding the opposite edge pays exactly $1/4$. The center $(1/2,1/2,0)$ has depth at least $1/2$ by symmetry of $\mu$. Moving its continuous coordinate by $h$ changes a through-mark cap by at most $4|h|/8$, since each nonvertical interval threshold moves by $h$ in magnitude and pure-base caps stay fixed. A containing cap contains its parallel through-mark cap. The two marks with base $(1/2,1/2)$ and continuous coordinates $\pm1/4$ therefore have depth at least $3/8$. Together with the four midpoint marks they show that $D$ is full-dimensional.

If $(z_0,x_0)\in C$ has $q_v(z_0)<3/10$, again take $\sigma x_0\ge0$. The containing cap $\sigma x-2q_v(z)\ge \sigma x_0-2q_v(z_0)$ excludes every other vertex fiber because its left side is at most $-1$ there and its right side exceeds $-3/5$. It pays length at most $1+2q_v(z_0)$ at $v$, so the mass is less than $1/5$. The four inequalities $q_v(z)\ge3/10$ therefore hold on $K$ and give $K\subseteq P_0$.

The extreme first-coordinate sections at $0$ and $1$ of $P_R$ remain those of $P_0$, namely the second-coordinate intervals $[3/10,7/10]$, since the new vertices have first coordinate $1/2$. These are the only possible integer first coordinates and neither section has an integer second coordinate. The quadrilateral with vertices $(0,1/2),(1/2,-R),(1,1/2),(1/2,R)$ lies in $P_R$ and has perpendicular diagonals of lengths $1$ and $2R$, so its area is $R$. The product containers contain $D$ and have volume at least $4R$.
statement:
Let $C=[0,1]^2\times[-1,1]$ and let $\mu$ be the sum of lengths on its four integer fibers, divided by $8$. Let $D$ be the ambient closed halfspace depth superlevel at $1/5$ for $\mu$. Then $D$ is compact, convex, full-dimensional, and disjoint from $\mathbb Z^2\times\mathbb R$. The maximum depth on the mixed trace of $C$ is $1/8$. The projection $K$ of $D$ is contained in the octagon
$$
P_0=\{z\in[0,1]^2:3/10\le z_1+z_2\le17/10,\quad |z_1-z_2|\le7/10\}.
$$
For every $R\ge1$, $P_R=\operatorname{conv}(P_0\cup\{(1/2,-R),(1/2,R)\})$ contains $K$, avoids $\mathbb Z^2$ even on its boundary, and has area at least $R$. The bounded ambient containers $P_R\times[-2,2]$ have unbounded volume and avoid the mixed lattice.
title: Unbounded lattice-free container volumes for a fixed actual depth region
